_doc: Layout for tools/civ_rebuild.py: RECONSTRUCTION, NOT ORIGINAL (docs/CIVILIZATION.md, 'Reconstruction (not original)').
No pixels here: page rectangles [page, x, y, w, h] (bytes of the 8 bpp view of SYSTEM/<page>), picture positions
in px (world (x, y) = px (x + 128, y - 40)), FMV mosaic rectangles, and the reason for each choice.
mosaics: name -> [movie, first frame, last frame]: the median mosaic of a BUNMEI.STR camera pan (1 FMV px = 1 picture px).
fmv_anchors: page -> [x, y, size, mosaic, mx, my]: page patch (x, y, size) registered at (mx, my) in the mosaic; it
gives the FMV colour of the patch's indices. Found by tools/civ_rebuild.py-independent search (per-index colour
variance, kept only when two neighbouring patches agree on the offset; strict = refined score < 0.07).
place: [piece | 'fmv:stamp', x, y, note]; a note starting '[fmv]' or '[nofmv]' limits the entry to that mode,
'flip' as first word mirrors it. Houses (index = TOPDOWN_TRIGGER_RECT_LISTS order): door = [x, width] px on the
south wall; draw = roof tileset + wall piece tiled along the front + door piece/stamp.

iron_grass.why: the only fully green 16x16 windows of A08000 (the lawn inside the double-gate cut-out)

iron_lawn.why: 24x24 windows of the FMV mosaic that are all green and within 10 of the sunlit lawn colour, so the ground continues the FMV's own grass

iron_stone.why: lowest-variance grey 16x16 windows of A08000 (room floors and wall faces); used for roofs and paving

wood_deck_page.why: deck planks of A06100 (the railing cut-out, x 512-590 y 64-95)

wood_deck.why: lowest-variance sunlit plank windows of the Lumberjack mosaic

stone_paving.why: the tan paving window of the Stonetown mosaic (its lawn and grey flagstone windows re-index badly in this CLUT, so they are not used)

stone_floor_page.why: the stone path cut-out of A07601 registered on the FMV (anchor 60,100)

stone_roof.why: the teal tiled roof cut-out of A07600 registered on the FMV (anchors 560-580, 60-80)

17.name: Iron Town
17.why_size: civ_sheets estimate (832 x 704); covers every house rectangle (H5 starts at px -23 and is clipped) and both exit rows

fmv.why: frames 61-91 pan down the town's central axis. Offset fixed by the code: the dome fills house H1 (px 305-398 x 163-296), the gate/dome/top-door axis is world x 223 (the centre of both exit rectangles), and the people baked into the FMV stand on residents #15 (blue hat), #6 (by the hut: 'go into this hut') and #7 (by the barrel)
fmv.why_erase: the FMV's own people (residents #15, #6, #7 and one at the left edge): the game draws its residents itself

houses.why: H1 is the dome: its dark arched doorway is at mosaic x 140-170 -> px 336-366
H2, east of the FMV: grey roof, the riveted wall cut-out along its front, the FMV's arched door
H3 ('the lift used to run on machinery'), top right
H5, the smith ('an iron gear?'), cut by the left edge of the picture as its rectangle is

place: real cut-out at its FMV match: the left gate of the double-gate cut-out registers on the round gate (anchor 648,60 -> mosaic 124,365); the panel's top 40 rows are cropped so the sign stays visible
the FMV fence (mosaic y 395-445) continued west with the real wall cut-out
pillar row like the FMV's at the courtyard edge (mosaic 0-110, 262-300)
mirror of the above on the west side
potted plants: the FMV has them along the upper terrace; ours mark the side streets
lamp poles beside the outer fence
[nofmv] the weathervane where the FMV shows it (mosaic 85-110, 130-200)
[fmv] the FMV's water barrel reused by the east lamp
solid: the 'Iron the No.1' building band (mosaic y 264-336): walk round it by the side streets
outer fence west of the gate
outer fence east of the gate
north wall west of the top door
north wall east of the top door

11.name: Lumberjack Town
11.why_size: civ_sheets estimate; holds the three houses, all patrols and the east exit (px x > 683)

fmv.why: frames 6-30 (windmill, tower, deck). Our alignment: the FMV's old man stands on resident #11 (sub 3, male resident, world 496,344 -> px 624,304); the hard-hat worker then falls 56 px east of #10's vertical patrol (x 280). Not pinned by the code as tightly as Iron Town
fmv.why_erase: the FMV's worker and old man

houses.why: H1, the workshop house of the two factory workers
H3, the raft maker's hut, drawn over the FMV's deck corner

solid: north edge west of the factory exit

16.name: Stonetown
16.why_size: civ_sheets estimate; holds the four houses, the west exit row (px y 480-489) and the boy at px (165,488)

fmv.why: frames 31-60 (teal roofs, white arch, keyhole well). Our alignment: the strong man on the tower stands on resident #2 ('Hup... HAAA!', a sub-3 lifter, px 272,292)

houses.why: H2 lies inside the FMV (its teal-roofed house)

place: the white arch cut-out marks the road to the north-east exit
solid: north edge west of the AREA16 s1 exit

17.why: H1 is the dome (93x133 px). This is the tall iron room with the copper pipe and round porthole (75x138), the only iron interior as tall as the dome; AREA18's page repeats it (A08600 13). Its resident (#5) has no dialogue
H2 (126x140, 'iron is sturdy' then 'you fixed the generator'): an iron room with a cabinet and stove that exists only on the AREA18 page; no other iron room is left for it
H3 ('the lift used to run on machinery'): the room whose chain runs up the wall to a pulley with a counterweight, i.e. a lift crank hut (Folkin's notes: Iron Town has crank huts for the lifts)
H4 (143x122, 'good material! wait a moment'): a workroom with a stool, a lamp and a coal basket, fitting a maker
H5, the smith who gives the iron gear: the widest iron room (143 px vs the 151 px rectangle), with a chain hoist and a hexagonal coal brazier, read as a forge

11.why: H1, the two factory workers ('now I can make something really interesting'): the log workshop with tools, a pot and stacked logs
H2 ('this machine is iron, I could use it'): the remaining wooden room (round table on a green rug); its footprint (124x105) is closest to H2 (111x101)

H3, by resident #4 who says 'a fortune-teller lives in this hut': the octagonal room with a 'ZZZ' sign and a plant on a table, the most ornate wooden room; its width (140) matches H3's (139). AREA18's page repeats it (A08600 15). The sitting resident #12 is in this house

16.why: H1, the largest house (124x135), where the strongman lives (#4: the gear and the generator): the largest stone room (chair, teal cabinet, stairs)
H2 (75x79, #12 with no dialogue): the remaining stone room (teal stool and table); it is far bigger than the rectangle, so it is drawn cropped
H3, the top-right house: the teal room with a wooden inner door, matching Folkin's 'locked closet in the top-right house'
H4, the craftsman ('I want to make something'): the room with shelves, jugs and a book, a workshop

_doc_interiors: interiors: town -> per house (1-based TOPDOWN_TRIGGER_RECT_LISTS index) the page rectangle of the matched room cut-out, a confidence (strong / plausible / guess) and the reasons. All matches are our guesses.
